The offline case asserts a unique complete canonical row, timestamp, identity, physical sequence and local visibility during a real HTTP 503, followed by an actual new send after service recovery.

The held-receipt case observes a real pending/dispatching local row, closes the first actual process lifetime, requires restarted Host POST replay with the original nonce, and asserts one canonical SQLite/UI message.

The held-receipt case creates new draft B through the editor, closes/reopens another actual lifetime, attempts release on the original already-closed socket, and requires B's full persisted draft and UI to remain unchanged before a new successful send.
Process identity is collected from observed owned processes, with Linux executable symlinks read only for those PIDs; the actual utility service, Rust Coordinator and AppHost parentage are asserted.

Normal shutdown refreshes the still-owned process-tree union before closing, then requires every observed identity to exit before reopen. Cleanup SIGKILL is separately recorded and cannot turn a failed graceful shutdown into a passed assertion.

Initial process-table or first-window failures share windowless cleanup/output capture; later failures retain page/console/process/HTTP/database diagnostics, failure trace/screenshot and explicit video capture attempts.

Each actual Electron launch opts into recordVideo, each context starts/stops tracing, each milestone captures DOM/PNG, and missing video or cleanup errors fail the case rather than being silently accepted.
The two cases assert no unexpected HTTP request and no captured pageerror, use zero retries, and contain no skip/fixme/only.
The harness requires GitHub Actions and full target HEAD equality, records hashes of actual assembled JS/native inputs, and requires Node >=22.16 for the readonly SQLite API.
